sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4,860.4 million in FY2016 to $14,342.9 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].
The path was a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue rose 89.1% in FY2021 to $16,071.7 million, then fell 24.3% in FY2022 to $12,172.9 million [D241][F6][D292][F7].
REGEN-COV contributed 66.4pp of FY2021 growth and its disappearance subtracted 36.3pp in FY2022 [D582][D585].
Since then growth has slowed to 7.8% in FY2023, 8.3% in FY2024 and 1.0% in FY2025, while operating margin fell 3.2pp in FY2025 to 24.9%, the window low [D342][D391][D440][D453][F30][D749].
In FY2025 net product sales fell 17.3% and subtracted 9.3pp from growth, while collaboration revenue grew 21.0% and added 9.0pp [D506][D507][D522][D523].
US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% and subtracted 14.2pp, which the filing attributes to competitive pressure, loss of share to compounded bevacizumab and the transition to EYLEA HD [D577][D578][P10].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits grew 33.6% and added 9.3pp, driven by higher Dupixent sales [D591][D592][P9].
Operating costs grew 4.4pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 5.4%, so operating income fell 10.3% against a 1.0% revenue gain [D464][D457][D441][D440].
Diluted EPS grew 8.2% against net income growth of 2.1% as the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D444][D442][D459].
Operating margin of 24.9% in FY2025 sits 9.7pp below the window median of 34.6% and 30.8pp below the FY2021 high of 55.7% [F30][D751][D750].
R&D took 4.7pp off the FY2025 operating margin as it rose to 40.8% of revenue, while SG&A added 2.0pp as it fell 8.6% [D465][D420][D466][D456].
The SG&A decline was primarily due to lower charitable contributions to Good Days [P5].
In FY2025 net margin of 31.4% sat 6.5pp above the 24.9% operating margin, as other income of $1,652.8 million lifted pre-tax income [F50][F30][X117].
Operating cash flow of $4,978.9 million was 1.11x net income in FY2025, against a window median of 1.09x [F80][F40][D428][D30].
Free cash flow of $4,080.5 million was 0.91x net income and a 28.4% margin, above the 26.4% window median [F100][F40][D429][D425][D757].
Capex of $898.4 million was 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A, the highest capex-to-revenue ratio since FY2020 [F90][F10][D424][D430].
Stock-based compensation of $993.7 million equalled 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431].
Net cash of $16,879.9 million was 117.7% of revenue in FY2025, against a peer median of -50.7% of revenue (n=8) [D434][D435][D781].
That net cash ranks at the 100th percentile of the peer group, with debt held flat at $1,985.9 million [D780][F187][D461].
Buybacks of $3,438.6 million plus dividends of $370.3 million absorbed 93.3% of free cash flow in FY2025 [X137][X140][D436][D437].
The buyback helped cut the diluted share count 5.6%, the largest reduction in the window [D459].
Operating margin has fallen four years running, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [R1][F26][F30].
The decline reflects a mix shift toward lower-margin collaboration profit shares and heavy R&D, so the FY2021 level looks unlikely to recur [R1].
FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table are later recasts: $5,145.6 million against $6,710.8 million first reported, and $6,557.6 million against $7,863.4 million [R2][F3][X3][F4][X4].
Growth and margins spanning those years mix two presentations, so the FY2018 revenue decline of 12.4% should not be read as reported [R2][D92].
Whether US EYLEA sales, $2,747.8 million in FY2025, fall further or stabilize, in the FY2026 10-K [S43].
Whether operating margin holds above the FY2025 window low of 24.9%, in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D749].
Whether R&D stays above the 34.6% window median of revenue, having reached 40.8% in FY2025, in the FY2026 10-K [D760][D420].
